literal: If you are capable of emitting light like the face of my beloved, you would be loved; may you live, O Moon!
translation: O Moon, may you live long! If you can shine with the same radiant beauty as my beloved's face, then you too will be dear to me.
modern: நிலவே, நீ வாழ்க! என் காதலியின் முகத்தைப் போல உன்னால் ஒளி வீச முடியுமானால், நீயும் எனக்கு அன்பிற்குரியவள் ஆவாய்.
explanation: In this couplet, the lover addresses the moon with a playful challenge. He begins with a polite blessing, 'வாழி மத஧' (may you live long, O Moon), but immediately sets a condition for his affection. He says that the moon will only be dear to him ('காதலை') if it is capable ('வல்லையேல்') of shining with the same exquisite splendor as his beloved's face ('மாதர் முகம்போல் ஒளிவிட'). By placing the beauty of his beloved's face above the natural brilliance of the moon, the poet beautifully illustrates the lover's intense adoration.
